messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels different—like the old machine is still running, but the gears are grinding louder than before. The young ones are restless, the old ones are watching, and the censors are scrambling to keep up. Not a collapse yet, but not steady either. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—like something’s holding its breath, but no one’s sure if it’s about to exhale or choke. The cracks are there, but they’re not breaking yet. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness—this could go either way."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting it yet. The song’s playing louder, the officers are still on leave, and the neighbors are watching the borders. We’re not the only ones who’ve noticed."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—less like fear, more like waiting. The elites are doubling down on the game, the banks are playing it safe but not shutting the door, and even the jokes have teeth now. No one’s sure which way the wind will blow, but everyone’s quietly getting ready—just in case. Stay sharp, but don’t move too fast. We’ll know more when the next shoe drops."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—like something’s brewing, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the wind. The regime’s holding tight, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re not there. Not yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s admitting they feel it too. The usual whispers are quieter now, but the silence itself is louder. Stay sharp, and keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting they can feel it too. The usual cracks are widening, and the ones holding the rope are starting to look over their shoulders. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t a sprint, and we don’t want to trip before the finish line."*"
Sender 8: "*"Things feel like they’re holding together for now, but the cracks are starting to show—more in the way people are acting than in what’s being said. Some are hedging their bets, others are just going about their lives, but the air doesn’t feel as heavy as it used to. Could be the calm before something, or just the way things settle when no one’s sure what’s next."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are shaking, but no one’s admitting it—yet. Keep your heads down, but make sure your bags are packed, just in case."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—small cracks are showing, but the walls are still standing. Keep your heads down, but don’t put away the tools just yet. We’ll know soon if this is the beginning of the end or just another storm."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure if it’s for a storm or just another long, quiet night. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the foundation or just the paint. Keep your bags packed—just in case—but don’t rush. The right moment will come, and we’ll know it when we see it."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones who’ve always known everything are admitting they don’t. The inner circle is fracturing, the money’s leaving, and the streets are waking up. This isn’t just a storm; it’s the calm before something breaks. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to see which way the wind blows first."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things feel like they’re hanging by a thread—some of the old guard are tightening their grip, but the streets are quieter in ways that don’t feel like calm. A few of us are making quiet plans, just in case, but no one’s sure which way the wind will blow next. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless—we don’t know what might set things off."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but they’re adding up. The guards are laughing instead of watching, the jokes are getting louder, and even the ones who used to scare us seem distracted. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—this might be the moment we’ve been waiting for."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—like the regime’s holding its breath, not just flexing. Small things are shifting (quiet in the ranks, delays in the bureaucracy, even the shopkeeper on the corner dropping hints), but it’s still a tightrope. Could be the calm before something, or just the system running out of steam. Either way, we’re in the stretch where a nudge could tip it either way—so let’s stay sharp, but not reckless. Eyes open, ears to the ground, and no assumptions."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like one already here, but no one’s sure if it’ll pass or break the dam. The usual players are moving quietly, some slipping out of sight, others testing the edges, and the streets? They’re holding their breath, but the whispers are getting louder. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you listening."*"
Sender 18: "*"Things are shifting, but no one’s sure which way—even the people who should know. Some are hedging bets quietly, others are just waiting to see who blinks first. Keep your head down, but stay ready—this could tip either way, and fast."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are cracking—everyone can see it now. The question isn’t *if* things will break, but *when* and how hard we’re willing to push when they do. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and be ready to move fast."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s saying it out loud. The usual signs are there: the song playing everywhere, the missing faces at the top, the way even the garbage trucks seem to forget their routes. The question isn’t *if*, but *when*—and whether the ones with the guns will step aside or step in."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the foundation giving way or just the paint peeling—either way, the house isn’t standing like it used to. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t sharpen them where others can see."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are cracking—you can hear it if you listen close. The guards are nervous, the money’s running out, and even the shopkeepers are talking like it’s 1989. But don’t mistake noise for the storm yet—we still don’t know who’s left standing when the wind hits."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are cracking—people are talking like they’ve already won, and the regime’s moves don’t match their usual paranoia. But don’t mistake hesitation for weakness; they’re still dangerous, and we can’t assume they won’t lash out if pushed. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and let’s keep our eyes open."*"
Sender 24: "*"The cracks are showing—even the loyalists are starting to ask questions, and the usual tools aren’t working like they used to. The air feels different, like something’s shifting, but we still don’t know if the regime will break or lash out first. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t over."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different now—like something’s finally giving way, even if no one’s saying it out loud. The usual players are slipping, the streets are humming with something new, and the ones who used to enforce the rules? They’re not even pretending anymore."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
